items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.text: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. items.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
items.text: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! items.title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
items.text: Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce coupling without a full rewrite. The platform uses domain components, Data Mapper patterns, typed builders, and ArchUnit tests to enforce boundaries. Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes. By Leela Kumili

It looks like this: The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette.
